subject: Invoice INV-2027-08-00123 — unexpected usage spike & VAT charge
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nim-retail.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: finance@nim-retail.com
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 13:12:00 +0000
Subject: Invoice INV-2027-08-00123 — usage and VAT questions

Hi Kimberly,

We received invoice INV-2027-08-00123 this morning and there are a couple of items that don't line up with our expectations. Month-over-month consumption jumped from ~3.2M tokens to ~18.1M tokens, and the total invoiced amount (including VAT) is €28,900 — that's an order of magnitude higher than normal.

We attached a quick export from our side (attached: 2027-08-19_nimbus_usage_export.csv) that shows our internal request counts and totals; those numbers show ~3.6M tokens for the same billing window. Can you confirm how you are counting tokens for the August 1–15 window?

Also, our EU VAT ID (NL123456789B01) is on file — we expected reverse-charge handling for intra-EU B2B billing. The invoice shows VAT applied at 20%. Please hold any collection actions while we resolve this.

We can jump on a short call if helpful — available this afternoon CEST.

Thanks,
Alex Morgan
Head of Finance, Nimbus Retail

Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 11:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: Invoice INV-2027-08-00123 — initial reconciliation

Kimberly / team — preliminary findings below after pulling the raw metering logs and tokenization traces for the invoice period (2027-08-01T00:00:00Z — 2027-08-15T23:59:59Z). Attaching a short report (redwood-billing-run-20270819-report.pdf).

Summary (high level):
- Total tokens billed in our system for the window: 18,145,623
- Distinct request_ids observed: 16,892, but there is a cluster of duplicated request payloads between 2027-08-17T13:22:04Z and 2027-08-17T13:45:31Z (UTC) where client retries and a replay job overlapped.
- Deduplicated tokens (removing obvious exact-request duplicates): 3,842,110 tokens attributable to normal traffic.
- Estimated duplicated tokens attributable to replay/retry storms: ~14,303,513 tokens.

Root cause indicators:
1) A third-party data migration job at Nimbus replayed archived prompt batches into the Redwood API without idempotency keys; that job had an automatic retry policy that replayed a subset of requests multiple times.
2) We also saw a short-lived client-side retry storm (HTTP 5xx responses) from an IP range matching Nimbus’ cloud region, producing 2–3x attempts for some requests.

Tax handling note: VAT was applied to the full invoice total because our billing pipeline did not detect a validated VAT ID in the most recent billing profile snapshot; the VAT ID appears on the signed SLA you provided, but there was a timing mismatch in profile sync on Aug 16.

Recommendation:
- Issue a pro forma credit for the duplicated token volume: 14,303,513 tokens => gross credit €22,450.00.
- Recalculate VAT on the net payable after the credit and reverse-charge the VAT portion where appropriate (requires confirmation of Vat ID validation from Nimbus).
- Replace INV-2027-08-00123 with an adjusted invoice and updated invoice link.
- Operational fixes: require idempotency keys on bulk ingestion endpoints (we’ll enable new guidance + server-side dedupe) and add a profile sync retry with verification for tax IDs.

Please confirm and I’ll push the credit and issue the updated invoice.

- Sean
Billing Operations, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nim-retail.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:03:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Invoice INV-2027-08-00123 — usage and VAT questions

Hi Alex — quick update and next steps.

Thanks again for flagging this and for sharing your export. We completed an internal reconciliation and identified two contributing factors (details below) that caused the large jump on the Aug invoice.

What happened
- A data migration process at Nimbus replayed archived batches into the Redwood API without idempotency keys. Several batches were replayed and, at the same time, a transient client-side retry storm retried a subset of requests (see attached report). This resulted in ~14.3M tokens being counted multiple times.

What we’re doing for you
1) We will issue a credit for the duplicated usage: gross credit amount €22,450.00 (credit memo will be applied to INV-2027-08-00123).
2) We will recalculate VAT after applying the credit and reverse the VAT portion where applicable. If you can confirm your VAT ID (NL123456789B01) is active for intra-EU reverse-charge, we’ll remove the VAT from the adjusted invoice.
3) Updated invoice and credit memo will be posted to your Redwood billing portal and I’ll email the new invoice link by EOD today (Aug 22).
4) Operational actions: Sean’s team will enable server-side protections for bulk ingestion endpoints (require idempotency key + server-side dedupe) and we’ll add a profile sync check to avoid tax-profile timing mismatches.

Additionally, as a goodwill gesture for the disruption and the billing friction, we’d like to apply a one-time 10% service credit to your September usage invoice.

Next step for you
- Please confirm the VAT ID status (NL123456789B01) so we can proceed with the VAT reversal. Also confirm any PO number you need on the adjusted invoice.

I’ve attached the Redwood reconciliation report for your records (redwood-billing-run-20270819-report.pdf) and the usage CSV you sent is attached to the thread.

Thanks — we’ll make this right.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Appreciate the responsiveness.
